newsitem.title: USA: Interiors sees higher revs from license.
newsitem.headline: Interiors sees higher revs from license.

text.p: Interiors Inc said on Tuesday that it expects increased revenues after it signed an exclusive licensing agreement to reproduce the artwork of James Rizzi in decorative accessories.

"The company expects to raise its revenues approximately 20 percent for fiscal 1996 as a result of this program and to further increase revenues in future years," Max Munn, president and chief executive, said in a statement.
Rizzi was an official artist commissioned by the Atlanta Committee of Olympic Games and will be the artist for the Montreaux Jazz Festival in Switzerland.
The company expects to distribute this product through its A.P.F. Master Framemakers Division as well as its Italia Collection subsidiary.

Also, Interiors said it will postpone for about one month the record date for the dividend payable on its cumulative preferred stock series A. The company pays a 10 percent dividend in common stock and feels its common stock is currently undervalued.
